svg.title: Capital Is Inventory and Runway, Not Revenue
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Capital Is Inventory and Runway, Not Revenue; subtitle: Four buckets allocate a $1,000,000 startup illustration.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values are dollar allocations totaling $1,000,000, within the canonical $100,000–$1,500,000 startup range. Allocation shares are 75%, 10%, 10%, and 5%. Endpoint comparisons apply those shares mechanically, not as forecasts. Capital allocation alone does not generate the canonical Conservative, Base, or Scaled revenue outcomes.; caption: The $750,000 acquisition bucket matches the illustrative twenty-position funnel. The $50,000 operating reserve covers about 16.7 months of the Base illustration's $3,000 recurring monthly spend, not the entire possible 36-month deal timeline.; stages: label: Acquisition principal and premiums; value: $750,000 allocated; 75% of startup capital; numeric value: 750000.0; detail: Fund certificate principal or deed purchase basis and any required premium without counting purchases as revenue. At $100,000 total capital this bucket is $75,000; at $1,500,000 it is $1,125,000.; label: Parcel diligence and enforcement reserve; value: $100,000 allocated; 10% of startup capital; numeric value: 100000.0; detail: Hold cash for inspections, title work, recording, notices, and exceptional enforcement matters. Reserve funding is not an immediate expense. Endpoint allocations are $10,000 and $150,000 respectively.; label: Liquidity and subsequent-tax reserve; value: $100,000 allocated; 10% of startup capital; numeric value: 100000.0; detail: Preserve uncommitted liquidity for delayed redemptions and underwritten subsequent-tax decisions. Do not assume every additional tax payment earns interest or preserves priority. Endpoint allocations are $10,000 and $150,000 respectively.; label: Operating cash runway; value: $50,000 allocated; 5% of startup capital; numeric value: 50000.0; detail: Fund recurring administration and contractor retainers while investment cash remains tied up. Endpoint allocations are $5,000 and $75,000; at the lower endpoint, size spend and commitments to available runway rather than assuming Base-case overhead fits.

rect.title: label: Acquisition principal and premiums; numeric value: 750000.0; value: $750,000 allocated; 75% of startup capital; detail: Fund certificate principal or deed purchase basis and any required premium without counting purchases as revenue. At $100,000 total capital this bucket is $75,000; at $1,500,000 it is $1,125,000.
